title: Iced Coffee Icebox Cake
changes_from_base: Thin chocolate wafers layered in a loaf tin with an espresso whipped cream and left to soften in the fridge, instead of sponge and ice cream.
summary: Layers of chocolate wafer biscuits soften between espresso-spiked whipped cream to create a rich, coffee-flavoured sliceable dessert, finished with dark chocolate curls.
equipment: stand mixer or hand mixer with whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
bar of dark chocolate, for shaving

steps.title: Whip
steps.text: Whip the 454 g double cream with 21-28 g icing sugar, the 1½ tsp instant espresso powder, 1 tsp vanilla and a pinch of salt on medium speed just until stiff peaks form, about 3-4 min, taking care not to overbeat.

steps.title: Line
steps.text: Line the loaf tin with cling film, leaving a generous overhang on all sides.

steps.title: Base
steps.text: Spread about 120 ml of the whipped cream in a 1 cm layer over the base, then cover with a snug single layer of the chocolate wafer biscuits, about 8 per layer.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread a thin layer of cream over the biscuits, add another layer of biscuits, and repeat until the 340 g of biscuits and all the cream are used, finishing with a layer of cream on top.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cover and chill for at least 24 h so the biscuits soften fully.

steps.title: Turn
steps.text: Invert the cake onto a plate, peel off the film and smooth any gaps with a hot, dry palette knife.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Shave curls from a bar of dark chocolate over the top using a peeler before slicing.

tips: Chill for the full 24 h so the biscuits soften right through to a cake-like texture.
Whip the cream just to stiff peaks to avoid a grainy texture when sliced.
Use a hot, dry palette knife to smooth any gaps once the cake is turned out.
storage: Keeps covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Contains caffeine.
